t.6.111.1: Permitted by Rāma, that unsurpassed aerial chariot flew up, like a great cloud driven upward by the wind.
t.6.111.2: Then Rāma, the delight of the Raghus, having cast his eyes all around, spoke to Sītā, the princess of Mithilā, whose face was like the moon.
t.6.111.3: Behold, Vaidehī, Laṅkā, fashioned by Viśvakarman, standing upon the peak of Trikūṭa, which resembles a summit of Kailāsa.
t.6.111.4: Behold this battlefield, Sītā, a mire of flesh and blood; here took place the great slaughter of the monkeys and the Rākṣasas.
t.6.111.5: For your sake, O large-eyed one, Rāvaṇa has been slain by me; here too Kumbhakarṇa was slain, and the night-roamer Prahasta.
t.6.111.7: Akampana has been slain, and other mighty rākṣasas too: Triśiras and Atikāya, and Devāntaka and Narāntaka.
t.6.111.6: Here Indrajit, the son of Rāvaṇa, was slain in battle by Lakṣmaṇa, and here too fell Virūpākṣa, dreadful to behold, along with Mahāpārśva and Mahodara.
t.6.111.8: Then his wife, named Mandodarī, surrounded by a thousand tearful co-wives, lamented over him.
t.6.111.9: And here can be seen the ford of the ocean, O lovely-faced one, where, having crossed the sea, we spent that night.
t.6.111.10: This is the bridge I had built across the ocean, that sea of waters, for your sake, O large-eyed lady: the bridge of Nala, a feat most difficult to accomplish.
t.6.111.11: Behold, Vaidehī, the ocean, the abode of Varuṇa, unshakable and boundless, roaring loudly and frequented by conches and pearl-oysters.
t.6.111.12: Behold, Maithilī, Hiraṇyanābha, the golden lord of mountains, who rose up splitting the ocean so that Hanumān might rest.
t.6.111.13: Here this Vibhīṣaṇa, king of the Rākṣasas, came.
t.6.111.14: Here, Sītā, is seen that Kiṣkindhā with its colorful forests, the delightful city of Sugrīva, where Vālī was slain by me.
t.6.111.15: Sītā, there can be seen that great Ṛśyamūka, the best of mountains, covered with golden minerals, like a cloud with lightning.
t.6.111.16: Here I met Sugrīva, the lord of the monkeys, and here, O Sītā, I made a pact with him for the slaying of Vālin.
t.6.111.17: Here is seen that Pampā, the lotus-filled lake with its colourful woods, where I, bereft of you, lamented in deep sorrow.
t.6.111.18: On her bank I saw Śabarī, who walked the path of dharma, and here I slew Kabandha, whose arms stretched a yojana long.
t.6.111.19: There in Janasthāna, O Sītā, that splendid tree can be seen where, for your sake, O charming lady, a great battle took place between the cruel Rāvaṇa and the great-souled Jaṭāyu.
t.6.111.20: Khara was slain in battle, and Dūṣaṇa was struck down, and the mighty Triśiras too, by me with straight-flying arrows.
t.6.111.21: There, too, is seen the bright leaf-hut, lovely to behold, where you were carried off by force by Rāvaṇa, lord of the rākṣasas.
t.6.111.22: Here is the lovely Godāvarī, auspicious, with its clear and tranquil waters; and there, indeed, the hermitage of Agastya can be seen. Look, Maithilī!
t.6.111.23: And here, O Vaidehī, is seen the great hermitage of Śarabhaṅga, where Śakra, the thousand-eyed Puraṃdara, came.
t.6.111.24: These are the hermitages of the ascetics that come into view, O slender-waisted one, where Atri, head of the family, dwells, radiant as the sun and fire. Here, O Sītā, you saw the female ascetic devoted to dharma.
t.6.111.25: In this place the huge-bodied Virādha was slain by me.
t.6.111.26: O lovely-limbed one, there shines Citrakūṭa, lord of mountains, where the son of Kaikayī came to win my favour.
t.6.111.27: Here, seen from afar, is that Yamunā with her many-hued forests, where this glorious hermitage of Bharadvāja shines forth.
t.6.111.28: Here the Gaṅgā, she who flows along three paths, comes into view, O lady of fair complexion; and this is Śṛṅgaverapura, where Guha came to meet us.
t.6.111.29: There, that is Ayodhyā coming into view, the royal capital of my father. O Vaidehī, now that you have returned, bow down in reverence to Ayodhyā.
t.6.111.30: Then all those vānaras and the rākṣasa Vibhīṣaṇa, leaping up again and again, beheld that city so beautiful to look upon.
t.6.111.31: Then the monkeys beheld that city Ayodhyā, garlanded with rows of white mansions, with spacious courtyards, crowded with elephants and horses, like Amarāvatī, the city of great Indra.
